Exercise A

too, enough, so and such

Think about the pattern: too / enough + adjective (+ to + verb), enough + noun, so + adjective and such + (a) noun. Choose the correct form for each gap.

Before you start — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking. You can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Twelve things that are too much, too little or just enough

1. The flat is far 1 small for four people.

2. The room isn’t big 2 for two desks and a bed.

3. There is more than 3 space for a desk and a sofa.

4. The seminar is 4 good to miss.

5. He speaks 5 quickly for most of us to follow.

6. She was 6 tired that she fell asleep during the seminar.

7. It was 7 a long journey that we booked a hotel.

8. I haven’t got 8 money to pay the deposit.

9. We received 9 complaints about the noise to ignore them.

10. The library is 10 to work in, but the chairs are uncomfortable.

11. The lecture was 11 less interesting than I had hoped.

12. At that moment she 12 the contract, so we waited outside.

Exercise B

Advice conversation

Breakout rooms, pairs, 12 minutes. One of you is the student, one the adviser. Talk first (English only), then each write a short follow-up here.

Choosing a course for next term

The student can take one elective. The adviser knows all three:

Public Speaking: Mondays 08:15 · 12 students · you give two talks · very practical.

Academic Writing: Wednesdays 17:00 · 35 students · about 80 pages of reading a week · one long essay.

Data Skills: Fridays 10:00 · 20 students · no talks, no essay · software you must install and learn alone.

Ask questions and give reasons. Use too, enough, so … that, such a … and at least two comparatives.

Word count: 0

Write 80–110 words. Then press Continue and exchange texts with your partner.

Exercise C

Check your partner’s text

Swap texts with your partner in the chat. Read your partner’s follow-up and write one useful tip.

Find one comparing phrase and one too / enough / so / such phrase. Then write one tip: something to add, or one thing to fix.
